pricingPrinciple: Solo artists stay cheap by default. Charge more only for real provider cost, storage/bandwidth pressure, payment/provider work, or hands-on custom build labor.

storefrontPolicy.principle: Let artists start tiny so adoption compounds, but cap free usage before it can become spam or provider-cost bleed.

foundingCoreMonth.label: Founding Core Artist Month
foundingCoreMonth.summary: Selected May 2026 core artists receive a no-charge artist universe/platform build, up to five launch songs packaged into their surfaces, hosting/maintenance, and platform-testing access in exchange for promotion and feedback.

artistManagementLane.defaultOwnerBoundary: Artist keeps masters, compositions, public likeness, and uploaded media unless a separate signed agreement says otherwise.
artistManagementLane.marketingLicenseBoundary: Uploaded artist media may be used to operate, display, preview, package, and promote the artist's services and platform surfaces, but not to create unrelated company profit outside the agreed service lane.

artistReferralProgram.eligibleRevenueBasis: onboarded spend actually received after refunds, chargebacks, taxes, processor fees, paperwork holds, and owner approval

songCreationPricing.name: Artist Cut

dawBetaAccess.name: DAW Beta
dawBetaAccess.summary: DAW access is free for every user through 2026 while the room remains beta-labeled.

agenticMarketingPush.baseDeliverable: 365-day content calendar with longform blog base, SkyeNet site publishing lane, Nexus feature slots, proof receipts, and approval workflow.
requires: publishing credentials or owned SkyeNet surface
provider budget for automation and media
separate social account credentials before social publishing claims
agenticMarketingPush.claimBoundary: The platform can sell and operate a proof-backed content production/publishing push; it cannot guarantee reach, virality, press, sales, playlisting, or social-platform acceptance.

fan_commerce_model.principle: Every artist page should be able to sell, collect support, prove fulfillment, and trail revenue back to a hashed artist ID.
fan_surfaces: single, EP, album, bundle, or private full-song package after preview playback
support/tip payments; do not call them charitable donations unless the legal/tax entity supports that claim
merch, tickets, meet-and-greet slots, fan passes, and behind-the-drop access
booking, media, feature, interview, or collaboration request cards
email/SMS capture routed into the 0S campaign engines

stripe_skyepay_tracking.artist_id_strategy: Store artist IDs internally and send a non-reversible HMAC/hash or opaque artist reference through checkout metadata.
stripe_skyepay_tracking.settlement_holder: Company Stripe/SkyePay lane collects fan payments first, then approved artist payouts are reviewed and batched.
stripe_skyepay_tracking.payout_cadence: biweekly after refunds, disputes, rights holds, paperwork, and provider costs are reviewed

artist_options: buyer_covers_platform_and_processing: fan pays artist price plus 13% platform fee plus estimated processing
platform_fee_on_top: fan pays artist price plus 13%; processing is deducted from settlement unless separately passed through
artist_absorbs: fan pays artist price; artist payout is artist price minus 13% platform fee minus Stripe/payment processing

example_199_single.note: Stripe domestic card pricing is commonly 2.9% + 30c in the US. Low-ticket drops should show the artist that the fixed 30c fee is material before launch.

legal_onboarding_lanes.vendor_seller: Use when the artist is selling music, merch, fan support, downloads, booking/media offers, or access products through the Nexus Shop.
legal_onboarding_lanes.independent_contractor: Use when Skyes Over London pays the artist for company-requested services such as founding-core promotion, testing, content, appearances, consulting, or deliverables.
legal_onboarding_lanes.both_possible: Some artists should complete both. Keep fan revenue/vendor payouts separate from company-paid contractor compensation.
paperwork_before_real_payout: vendor/seller agreement or independent contractor agreement as applicable
payout profile or Stripe Connect account when automated transfers are used

fan_commerce_model.business_growth_lane: Founding Nexus artists can be routed into the greater 0S business setup, docs, campaigns, email, and incorporation-support surfaces with a 67% eligible-feature discount where approved.

truth_rules: Every artist page should include a Nexus Shop lane for purchases, support/tips, private full access, merch/booking, and fan capture where the artist scope supports it.
Fan checkout metadata should trail to an artist ID hash, drop ID, SKU ID, fee policy, Stripe/SkyePay IDs, fulfillment route, and payout batch state.
The default platform fee is 13%; artists can choose buyer-covered or artist-absorbed pricing, but the 13% company fee must be respected.
Company-held fan payments should settle through payout review with paperwork, rights, disputes, refunds, provider costs, and owner approval before artist payout release.

Artist vendor/seller paperwork and independent-contractor paperwork are separate lanes; some artists may need both depending on whether they sell through the platform and also perform services for the company.
Artist management/exclusive lanes do not transfer music ownership, distribution authority, royalty collection, or licensing authority unless a separate signed agreement says so.
Qualified SkyeMusicNexus artist referrals use a 40% payout policy against onboarded spend after refunds, chargebacks, taxes, processor fees, paperwork holds, and owner approval.
